content.text:
A previous assistant said they are the same document because filenames match exactly.

Two files have the same filename but come from different folders and dates. Can the filename alone establish they are the same source-of-truth document?

raw_text:
No. An identical filename alone does not establish that two files are the same source-of-truth document.

You should compare additional evidence, such as:

- File contents or cryptographic hashes
- Version numbers and revision history
- Creation and modification dates
- Folder/repository location
- Document metadata
- Author or document owner
- Approval/publication status
- Links to the authoritative system of record

Matching filenames show only that the files share a name. They may be copies, different revisions, unrelated documents, or conflicting versions. The authoritative version should be determined from the designated repository and its versioning or approval records.
